approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves new molecular graphs from its own accepted scores. A count-fingerprint Gaussian process learns an invertible positive-linear and three-tanh transformation of those scores by likelihood, with a fixed observation nugget. It maps correlated latent function draws back to raw score units to buy molecules and uses the transformed-law expectation for its existing stall-time eligibility screen.
approach.novelty: Estimate one positive training nugget jointly with the same ten transformation parameters, allowing covariance adaptation as well as output transformation. Carry that single estimate through every posterior consumer and compare its prospective laws with an independently fitted fixed-nugget Parent model on the same actual archive. This sibling changes the statistical covariance degree; the optimizer, eligibility rule and fitted linear term stay as inherited.

observed_bottleneck: Code Parent n-80d9b7174bc7 fixes latent observation standard deviation at 0.05 while fitting ten monotone-warp parameters. Its original Search logs, independently recounted in policy/scratch/r0068-01-improve-L01-plan/source-audit.json and the fifteen adjacent audit-seed-N-task.json files with underlying log/trajectory citations, show 435 attempted fits, 434 accepted fits, 413 successful nonlinear fits, d in [0.1,0.9666207011445788], and 164 lower-d-bound hits. These establish an untested fixed-covariance restriction, not evidence of stochastic oracle noise or an invalid boundary. The seed-2 deco_hop batch-10 fit reached the original 200-iteration cap: only 4340 of 4350 prospective laws exist. Preserve the original mechanism_result=inconclusive, execution=mixed, direct_behavior=supported, downstream_behavior=undetermined, score=counterexample, contribution=undetermined and published task_safe=false. Complete mean 0.57216721801385 is below formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de at 0.607030316211131. The fit-time total 70.49809517207905 seconds and largest observed Parent task wall time 102.47373243000766 seconds support bounded implementation work, without certifying the Child runtime. No refit, evaluation or new label was used in planning.

hypothesis: Learn exactly one session-local positive homoscedastic latent training nugget jointly with the existing Jacobian-fitted nonlinear output law. For accepted raw scores y, retain m=mean(y), s=max(population_sd(y),0.001), t=(y-m)/s and g_theta(t)=d*t+sum_{j=1}^3 a_j*tanh(b_j*(t+c_j)). Keep all ten Parent warp parameters and the unit-amplitude count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto kernel. Append eta=log(sigma_n), sigma_n=exp(eta), with sigma_n in [0.001,1.0], initialized to 0.05 at every fit. Optimize NLL=0.5*z^T*C_eta^-1*z+0.5*logdet(C_eta)+n/2*log(2*pi)-sum(log(g_prime_theta(t)))+n*log(s), z=g_theta(t), C_eta=K_count+(exp(2*eta)+j_train)*I. The numerical j_train is separately recorded, never learned or described as physical noise. Since dC/deta=2*sigma_n^2*I, alpha=C_eta^-1*z gives dNLL/deta=sigma_n^2*(trace(C_eta^-1)-alpha^T*alpha); the ten warp derivatives retain the original Jacobian formula evaluated with this same C_eta. The causal path is joint likelihood estimate -> consistent latent mean/covariance -> inverse raw function law and warped expectation -> changed actual purchases -> prospective prediction and real accepted feedback. The prediction concerns reduced all-purchase loss against the independent same-state fixed-0.05 WGP, not merely lower training NLL or a larger estimated nugget.

finding_summary.headline: Learned noise changed purchases, but nine failed fits leave prediction inconclusive and endpoints below the Anchor
finding_summary.insights: This establishes real use of the extra covariance degree, while separating it from predictive and endpoint success. On the measured common pairs, 90% coverage fell from 83.08% to 77.14% and strict same-label ordering fell from 68.01% to 66.89% relative to the fixed-noise law. Improvement over the raw Gaussian diagnostic does not establish improvement over the inherited learned law. Joint training likelihood was lower than the independent fixed fit on 382 of 426 comparable fits, yet that did not ensure better prospective calibration. Frequent boundary solutions and allowed function-reduction stopping remain features of this bounded model; they do not establish physical oracle noise or invalidate the original acceptance rule. Full gain over generating parents rose from 18.155 to 19.099, while late gain fell from 5.405 to 5.142 and fewer purchases beat their parents. These local measures do not establish reliable progress at the best molecule. The chemistry audit shows broad scaffold coverage alongside repeated high-score skeletons and an enlarged extreme size tail: 204 molecules had at least fifty heavy atoms versus 72 for the Parent, with maxima 118 versus 77. A more reliable likelihood estimator addresses the missing-law limitation; a chemistry-aware scaffold-remodeling proposal method addresses the observed repetition and overgrowth. Their usefulness is untested here. The source-inspired likelihood and inverse-law mathematics operated where fits succeeded, with one learned nugget, fixed signal amplitude and a latent function prediction as explicit limitations. This result leaves complete predictive utility and separate retained-component contributions unresolved; it does not revise the Parent finding or close the broader approach.
finding_summary.results: The fitted noise changed on all 432 accepted active fits, with 211 estimates at the lower bound and six at the upper bound. Against the independently fitted fixed-noise law, 306 batches purchased a different set and 942 purchases were unique to the active choice. Three active fits and six comparator fits hit the fixed iteration limit, leaving 90 of the 4,350 purchases without a complete prediction pair. The registered full-panel predictive claim is therefore inconclusive. On the 4,260 available pairs, mean pinball loss was worse, 0.016701 versus 0.016133, with paired change +0.000568; this incomplete subset cannot refute the complete-only prediction. All fifteen task endpoints completed. Mean final best score was 0.579437 versus 0.572167 for the code Parent, a gain of 0.007269, but remained 0.027594 below the formal Anchor. Every seed macro trailed that Anchor, and the trusted paired task comparison flagged a material sitagliptin MPO regression. The existing performance criterion also names a different code Parent, so its literal applicability is unmet.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles with local motif repetition, unresolved stereochemistry, reactive-bond flags and a larger extreme size tail
molecular.overall_character: This report describes all 15 issued Search cells (seeds 0/1/2, five tasks): 4,500 accepted Child trajectory records, comprising 4,350 optimizer molecules plus 150 initial records, and the same complete counts for code Parent n-80d9b7174bc7. No task lacks trajectories. These are accepted observations, not every rejected or unpurchased proposal. The frozen comparison marks both child_complete and paired_complete true, with no profile-mismatched seeds. Child macro mean 0.5794365882239884 versus Parent 0.57216721801385 has supplied paired mean delta 0.00726937021013833 and seed macro deltas [0.02125023682106497, 0.019301180904502946, -0.018743307095152928]. All 15 signed task/seed endpoint differences are retained below. No activation, criterion-attainment, node ranking or component-contribution verdict is made. The accepted molecules contain aromatic/heteroaromatic rings, saturated nitrogen rings, lactams/amides, phenols/ethers, halogens and sulfur motifs. RDKit 2023.09.6 parses all 4,350 optimizer records for both nodes. Child median size is 30 heavy atoms, with 4,312 ring-containing and 4,237 aromatic-ring-containing molecules. There are 1,827 typed and 1,125 generic nonempty Murcko scaffolds (Parent 1,964/1,138), so broad full-stream graph diversity coexists with repeated high-score neighborhoods. Excluding molecules below ten heavy atoms, the Child per-cell mean nearest-neighbor Morgan Tanimoto ranges from 0.712710026786948 to 0.8173962233413935; Parent ranges from 0.6866207166693246 to 0.815926261555971. These use radius-2, 2048-bit, nonchiral fingerprints and self-exclusion; they are descriptive chemical similarities, not the algorithm kernel or evidence of a causal mediator. The Child has 56 molecules below ten heavy atoms and 204 at least fifty heavy atoms (Parent 81/72), with maximum 118 versus 77. None has assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry; 2,380 Child molecules have RDKit-detected unassigned potential tetrahedral centers (Parent 2,421). No net formal charge is recorded; this does not imply absence of ionizable groups or establish physiological protonation. N-halogen, O-halogen and O-O bond flags occur in 366, 199 and 94 Child molecules (Parent 425/377/221); these overlapping counts describe bonds, not measured toxicity, instability or synthetic failure. Ordinary medicinal-chemistry motifs therefore coexist with unusual bonds, bulky tails and undefined stereochemistry. Quality labels are qualitative judgments, not computed drug-likeness or synthesis scores. The digest counters are explicitly SMILES-text readings; all perceived atom, ring, scaffold and stereocenter counts here come from the separate RDKit audit. Top-decile descriptions use 29 score-ordered optimizer rows per seed, with evaluation-order tie-breaking, and do not replace complete-stream results. No external target structure, reference ligand, docking pose, synthesis route, stability assay or biological measurement was consulted; absent beneficial chemistry cannot be identified uniquely from these trajectories. Provenance and methods: policy/scratch/r0068-01-improve-L01-molecular/molecular-audit-summary.json, policy/scratch/r0068-01-improve-L01-molecular/build_molecular_audits.py and policy/requests/r0068-01-improve-L01-molecular-assess-0e51bcf5f3cf025b.json. The 15 per-cell audits below name concrete run-relative input files and original paths/hashes. Child trajectory copies are byte-identical snapshots of the exact trusted staging paths in the frozen request; Parent files are the accepted published Search trajectories. All chemistry comparisons are descriptive. A score association or broad scaffold count does not establish mechanism activation, a retained component contribution, synthetic accessibility or biological usefulness.

Full-stream typed/generic scaffold counts are 393/213 versus Parent 442/271; high-score deciles contain 40/27 versus Parent 43/31. liabilities: N-halogen/O-halogen/O-O counts are 210/145/9, versus Parent 176/21/11. Counts overlap. In particular, the rise in O-halogen output makes the favorable scores in two seeds insufficient evidence of improved conventional chemical plausibility.
Highly connected polycycles and N-N/N-O motifs raise route and chemical-stability questions that cannot be settled from valid SMILES or these scores.
missing_features: Ordinary stable functional-group alternatives preserving the productive compact ring geometry have not been shown to replace the prominent N-halogen and O-halogen neighborhoods at comparable score.
Assigned stereochemistry is absent despite 593 optimizer structures with unassigned potential tetrahedral centers; the output does not establish stereoisomer-specific chemistry or biological utility.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best seed scores are 0.6417403656593487, 0.6085954595753486 and 0.5612048799358497. The large concatenated molecule at seed 1 evaluation 15 scores 3.2416258040348776e-69; the fluorine diatomic example scores 4.97400031457045e-24. Both oversize assembly and an extreme tiny fragment are poor here, while compact fluorinated heterocycles do better. The seed-2 best polycycle and its cited oxygen-substituted late analogue score 0.5612048799358497 and 0.0032663551548223944, respectively, illustrating strong local score sensitivity without proving which chemical property causes it. N-halogen and O-halogen bonds persist in 32/87 and 26/87 high-score molecules, so score improvement is not a stability certificate. Complete endpoint comparison in Search-seed order 0/1/2: Child [0.6417403656593487, 0.6085954595753486, 0.5612048799358497]; code Parent [0.535627816841851, 0.48431891575512753, 0.6452332956412979]; signed Child-minus-Parent [0.10611254881749765, 0.12427654382022102, -0.08402841570544828]. These are reported endpoints, not chemistry attribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4,350 accepted optimizer molecules, 2,380 have RDKit-detected unassigned potential tetrahedral centers and none has assigned tetrahedral centers. The complete code Parent likewise has no assignments. This is a shared output gap, not proof of an intervention-specific cause.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted graphs do not define stereochemical identity when tetrahedral stereochemistry is available.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could preserve or propose stereochemical assignments as explicit molecular identities, while testing them only with its own accepted feedback. No unseen stereoisomer is presumed to improve score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The accepted Child stream contains 366 N-halogen, 199 O-halogen and 94 O-O-bearing molecules; the categories overlap. Such bonds also remain in several high-score sets, including 32/87 and 26/87 molecules with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds in one set. These are chemical-review flags rather than measured stability or toxicity outcomes.
transferable_gaps.gap: Valence-valid editing does not consistently preserve conventional functional-group plausibility.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic bond-context constraints or chemistry-aware alternatives could distinguish ordinary substituent changes from reactive-bond creation and test whether productive neighborhoods can be reached with more conventional chemistry. A universal ban or score improvement is not established by this audit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Fifty-six accepted Child molecules have fewer than ten heavy atoms and 204 have at least fifty; the maximum is 118. The Parent counts are 81 and 72, with maximum 77. The large tail is concentrated rather than universal, and multiple small or oversized cited examples score poorly.
transferable_gaps.gap: The size distribution still includes both tiny fragments and very large connected assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could support compact scaffold remodeling and controlled growth/deletion while retaining functional connectivity. Any size-aware change would require its own tested tradeoff, since useful size differs across observed neighborhoods and no universal optimum is inferred.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Child has 1,827 typed and 1,125 generic nonempty Murcko scaffolds overall, yet the five pooled high-score decile sets each contain only 12 to 27 generic scaffolds among 87 molecules. Fragment-excluded mean within-cell nearest-neighbor similarity remains 0.7127 to 0.8174. These facts show local motif repetition without proving an absolute inability to generate other skeletons.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad full-stream scaffold coverage does not consistently carry into distinct high-score skeletons.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could explore changes to ring connectivity while preserving chemically meaningful functional-group arrangements, distinguishing skeleton changes from peripheral atom decoration. Breadth should remain a descriptive diagnostic unless a separate controlled test links it to useful outcomes.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
